top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards targeted protein degradation as a simple, new chemical principle (a small molecule bringing a ubiquitin ligase and a target into one ternary complex for catalytic, event-driven removal) that has been reproduced independently and has real consequences. The allocation rests on distinct, datable discoveries: Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept and proof of principle, and Handa for identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target, which anchors the molecular-glue strand and most clinical degraders. The citation on recruiting ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins covers both strands honestly. P003 is a close second but leaves the glue strand unnamed, and I read Ciulli's VHL and cooperativity work as a rigorous refinement of an existing concept. P002 is mature and elegant but a sequel to the 2010 cross-coupling prize with less new science; any award is preferred to none.
